_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Guatemala covering Maya civilization heartland (Tikal, El Mirador, Kaminaljuyú), Classic Maya collapse, K'iche'/Kaqchikel kingdoms (Popol Vuh), Alvarado conquest, colonial Antigua capital, Captaincy General of Central America, independence 1821, liberal/conservative struggles, Ubico dictatorship, 1944 October Revolution, Arbenz reforms/1954 CIA coup (United Fruit Company), 36-year civil war 1960-96 (200,000 dead, Mayan genocide under Ríos Montt), and Rigoberta Menchú.

religion.note: Highly syncretic Catholicism (Maximon/San Simón folk saint); evangelical explosion since 1976 earthquake; Ríos Montt was Pentecostal (used religion to justify war); Maya spiritual practices (ajq'ij daykeepers, ceremonies at Tikal/Iximché); Semana Santa processions (Antigua, largest in Americas)

ethnic_groups.name: Mestizo/Ladino
ethnic_groups.notes: Mixed or culturally assimilated; Spanish-speaking; urban and eastern; 'ladino' identity distinct (adopted Western culture regardless of ancestry); historically dominant politically/economically

ethnic_groups.name: Maya
ethnic_groups.notes: K'iche' (largest, Popol Vuh), Kaqchikel, Mam, Q'eqchi', 22 groups total; ~6M; descendants of Classic Maya civilization; highlands; corn/milpa agriculture; traje (traditional dress); suffered genocide 1981-83 (Ríos Montt, scorched earth, 626 massacres documented); Rigoberta Menchú (Nobel 1992); CICIG anti-corruption

ethnic_groups.name: Xinca
ethnic_groups.notes: Non-Maya indigenous; southeastern; nearly extinct language; distinct from Maya peoples

ethnic_groups.name: Garífuna
ethnic_groups.notes: Afro-Caribbean-Arawak; Livingston (Caribbean coast); drumming/Punta; UNESCO intangible heritage; arrived from Honduras/St. Vincent

ethnic_groups.name: Other (White, foreign)
ethnic_groups.notes: Spanish descent; German coffee planters (Alta Verapaz, 19th century); Korean, Chinese small communities

country_profile.notes_unique: Heartland of Maya civilization (Tikal, El Mirador - largest pyramid by volume); Popol Vuh (K'iche' Maya creation text); Antigua Guatemala (UNESCO, colonial capital destroyed by earthquakes); 1954 CIA coup against Arbenz (United Fruit Company, Cold War paradigm for Latin American interventions); 36-year civil war 1960-96 (~200,000 dead, 83% Maya); Ríos Montt convicted of genocide (overturned); Rigoberta Menchú (Nobel Peace 1992); most populous Central American country; quetzal bird (national symbol, endangered); Semana Santa; extreme inequality; migration to US

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

current_leader.name: Bernardo Arévalo
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: Movimiento Semilla; anti-corruption; son of Juan José Arévalo (1944 revolution president); nearly blocked from taking office by corrupt elites; diplomat; sociologist

former_leaders.name: Alejandro Giammattei
former_leaders.notes: Vamos; conservative; COVID; corruption; migrant deal with US; tried to block Arévalo's inauguration

former_leaders.name: Jimmy Morales
former_leaders.notes: FCN-Nación; comedian; 'neither corrupt nor a thief' (campaign); expelled CICIG (UN anti-corruption commission); family corruption

former_leaders.name: Otto Pérez Molina
former_leaders.notes: Patriota; general; resigned and arrested for customs fraud (La Línea scandal); first sitting president arrested; Kaibil special forces background

former_leaders.name: Álvaro Colom
former_leaders.notes: UNE; centre-left; social programs (conditional cash transfers); accused of corruption post-office

former_leaders.name: Efraín Ríos Montt
former_leaders.notes: De facto military ruler; scorched earth campaign against Maya (genocide conviction 2013, overturned on technicality); evangelical; most destructive period of civil war; ~40,000 killed in 17 months; died 2018

former_leaders.name: Jacobo Árbenz
former_leaders.notes: Agrarian reform (land redistribution from UFC); overthrown in CIA coup 1954 (Operation PBSUCCESS); most consequential Cold War intervention in Americas; died in exile

former_leaders.name: Juan José Arévalo
former_leaders.notes: Philosopher-president; 1944 October Revolution; labor code; social security; 'spiritual socialism'; 25 coup attempts survived
